correctness.rationale: For the exact 5-by-5 additive binary convolution operator, its Fourier range is the nonzero signed-derangement-permanent frequency set. A spanning-tree gauge identifies an 11-bit quotient and 14-dimensional uniform fibers. Both integer permanent algorithms agree in all 2048 cases; fast Walsh and direct character sums independently agree on all 2048 support-transform coefficients. The new nine-level histogram sums to 27996 in absolute values, giving 6999/512. Translation averaging proves no arbitrary projection can improve either endpoint norm.

value.rationale: The minimum endpoint projection norm is a canonical Banach-space stability invariant for the naturally singular convolution operator. The known signed-permanent magnitude histogram and 44-character Fourier projection norm do not determine this new 1710-class nonzero-support transform. The evaluated value 6999/512, with optimality over all projections, reveals stronger range-instability than the known 1269/256 norm for the original derangement-character band.
